opportunities.title: Initia Got Hacked Twice in Three Weeks. That's Not Bad Luck, That's a Pattern.
opportunities.why_now: A second exploit on the same protocol inside a month is a textbook case of unpatched root causes getting ignored after the first headline fades.
opportunities.angle: Incident-pattern breakdown: compare the two Initia exploits side by side, show what wasn't fixed, and argue 'second hack' should be a standing red flag category for traders and allocators.

opportunities.title: Across Protocol Didn't Get Smart-Contract Hacked — Someone Just Took Its Domain
opportunities.why_now: A live bridge warning users to avoid its own app because hackers hijacked the website, not the code, is a sharp reminder that DNS is still the weakest link in DeFi security.
opportunities.angle: Explainer/op-ed on domain-layer attacks as the new frontend exploit vector, with a checklist for verifying you're on the real dApp before signing anything.

opportunities.title: CertiK Says Exchanges Need Hard Dollar Caps on Hot Wallets. After $6.3B and $49M, Why Is This Still a Suggestion?
opportunities.why_now: CertiK's proposal lands days after both the Binance mega-hack fallout and Mercado Bitcoin's $49M breach, making the 'why wasn't this mandatory already' question unavoidable.
opportunities.angle: Policy-leaning breakdown of the hot-wallet-cap proposal, with a back-of-envelope on what caps would have actually prevented in recent incidents.

opportunities.title: Binance's iOS Warning Is a Reminder: Your Keys Were Never as Safe as the App Store Made You Feel
opportunities.why_now: A platform-level flaw that could expose wallet keys on a major exchange's mobile app is a direct hit to the self-custody-vs-CEX debate this community lives in.
opportunities.angle: Security-first breakdown of the flaw, what it means for mobile signing generally, and a hard recommendation list (hardware wallets, app permissions, key isolation).

opportunities.title: Near AI's Breach Just Showed What Happens When You Give Agents Wallets and Skip the Audit
opportunities.why_now: An AI-agent platform leaking user data and agent details lands right as the industry races to let autonomous agents hold keys and execute trades — a preview of the next hack category.
opportunities.angle: Forward-looking security take: use the Near AI breach as the opening case study for a 'AI agents are the next attack surface' thesis piece, with predictions on what gets exploited first.
